headline: Growth accelerates past guidance, profit streak extends
summary_short: Chime's Q2 2026 revenue rose 27% y/y to $669.8M, exceeding guidance, while net income of $27.9M marked a second consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability; the company raised its FY2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA outlook.
summary_long: Revenue grew 27% y/y to $669.8M, ahead of guidance, on 48% platform-revenue growth and Chime Prime-driven payments growth (+17% y/y to $430M). Net income of $27.9M marked a second straight GAAP-profitable quarter, largely reflecting a collapse in stock-based compensation versus the SBC-heavy year-ago IPO-vesting quarter. Adjusted EBITDA reached $101.6M (15% margin). Active Members grew 20% y/y to 10.4M. Cash fell to $536.0M q/q on $222.1M of YTD buybacks, partly offset by a $50M warehouse-facility draw. Chime raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.725–2.745B and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $465–475M; Q3 guidance calls for $680–690M revenue. CFO Matt Newcomb is departing Aug. 7, 2026; President Mark Troughton becomes interim CFO.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by Chime Prime accelerating Purchase Volume and payments revenue (+17% y/y to $430M, +21% with Outbound Instant Transfer), plus platform-related revenue growing 48% y/y to $240M.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded more than 12 points y/y to 15%, a 60% incremental margin, as revenue grew faster than operating expenses.
The swing to profit mainly reflects stock-based compensation and payroll tax collapsing to $71.2M from $928.1M a year earlier, when pre-IPO awards vested.
Total operating expenses fell to $573.6M from $1,391.7M, driven by the same stock-based-compensation step-down across technology, sales, and G&A lines post-IPO.
Chime Prime fueled acceleration in Active Member growth; the company added roughly 200,000 net new members q/q, twice its typical pace for a seasonally slower second quarter.
Cash fell q/q on $222.1M of YTD share repurchases and other financing outflows, partly offset by a $50M draw on the newly established warehouse facility.

CEO cites Chime Prime adoption, MyPay and Instant Loans momentum, and new Chime Enterprise employer partnerships (Allied Universal and a large national retailer) as growth drivers; CFO Matt Newcomb is departing, with President Mark Troughton named interim CFO.
